sources.notes: A plain curl (even with a full browser User-Agent) reliably gets a Radware/ShieldSquare 'Captcha Page' from every www.federal.bank.in URL, but this project's own fetchDoc (Node fetch/undici) reached the real page repeatedly while building and live-checking this adapter on 2026-09-27 -- likely a TLS/HTTP client fingerprint difference, not an absolute block. Fixture is a genuine trim of that live response. No bulk (>=Rs 3 crore) source is listed: the 'HVD Web Interest' PDF's href IS discoverable on this page, but fetching that specific document (a different /documents/10180/<folderId>/... path than the one that works) returns Radware's block page even via fetchDoc -- a gap to retry from GitHub Actions/VPS, not a guess.

Same client-dependent Radware behaviour as federal-bank:fd (see its notes) -- fixture is a genuine trim of a live fetchDoc response from 2026-09-27. The Rs 50 crore-<Rs 200 crore slab is deliberately left out of the parsed result: its own published sub-rates don't reconcile with the slab's own balance range (see reconcileNestedRates in federal-bank.ts) -- a real inconsistency on the bank's own page (it repeats a 'for balance less than Rs 10 crore' sub-clause inside a slab that starts at Rs 50 crore), not something we should guess at.
Verified against a live fetch (2026-09-27, HTTP 200, real table markup). One combined page also carries the bulk, RD and savings tables used by the other hdfc-bank.* adapters below.

sources.termsNote: The >=Rs 5 crore table has no senior-citizen column at all (only General, across ten amount sub-bands) — confirmed by checking the raw page for any 'Senior' text near that table.
sources.notes: Verified against a live fetch. Not covered: the separate 'Non-Withdrawable' (non-callable) table for >=Rs 2 crore on the same page, and the linked historical-rate PDF archives (one ~19MB) — out of scope for this pass.

Explicit RD table (not derived from FD). Published with one 'Effective From' date PER TENURE rather than one date for the whole table; the card uses the latest such date and flags the (few) tenures revised earlier on the row itself.
Flat 2.50% across all balances (no slabs) as of this fetch.

The page's own table is rendered client-side from a JSON API named in a data-api attribute (discovered fresh each run, never hardcoded — see icici-bank.ts). Verified against a live fetch of both the HTML page and the JSON it points at. No bulk-deposit source: no dedicated >=Rs 2-3 crore domestic FD rate page or JSON endpoint was found on icici.bank.in (a guessed /fixed-deposit/bulk-deposits URL 404s); the FD JSON also carries 8 additional undocumented tabs (interestData[1..8]) beyond the retail one used here, with no amount/tab label found for any of them, so they are not used rather than guessed at.
Own dedicated JSON API (distinct from the FD one — RD has narrower tenure bands), discovered from the page the same way as FD.
Flat 2.50% across all balances (no slabs) as of this fetch, read directly from the HTML table (no JSON API involved for this page).

Verified against a live fetch. One page also carries the >=Rs 3 crore tables used by indusind-bank.bulk below. No RD source: the dedicated Recurring Deposit page has zero <table> elements (a single marketing headline number only), and the bank does not state RD=FD anywhere found, so it's a gap rather than a guess.
Only Rs 3-5 crore (callable + non-callable) is on this page; no table was found for >=Rs 5 crore (the page instead says those rates are quoted per-deposit and valid only the day of booking).

sources.termsNote: Slabs below Rs 5 crore are incremental; the bank's own footnote says slabs from Rs 5 crore up are 'Flat Rate applicable on entire balance' (see each slab's note). Bands above Rs 1400 crore are MIBOR-linked with no fixed percentage printed and are not included.

sources.notes: Every rate table is a PDF whose dated file name changes on revision without the old URL ever redirecting or 404ing (it just stops being linked), so this source is the stable 'Interest Rates' index page; the adapter discovers the current Retail Deposits PDF link from it each run (via cheerio, not regex — one link's label has an un-escaped '>' that breaks naive <a> regexes, see idfc-first-bank.ts) and fetches that PDF with ctx.fetch. The same PDF also carries an explicit RD table (not derived from FD) plus Tax Saver and Green Deposit rows, all folded into this one adapter's output.

Discovers and parses the current Bulk Deposits PDF (Rs 3 crore and above), sections (I) and (II) only (Rs 3-27.50 crore, non-callable and callable). Sections (III)/(IV) for amounts above Rs 27.50 crore (ten narrower sub-bands, abbreviated 'crs.' labels, inline '<=' ranges) are not parsed — a follow-up, not a guess, given how few depositors reach that size.

sources.termsNote: The bank calls its slab method 'progressive'; its own worked example (Rs 10 lakh balance: 2.50% on the first Rs 3 lakh, 7.00% on the remaining Rs 7 lakh) is the domain model's 'incremental' method.
sources.notes: Discovers the current Savings Deposits PDF from the index page. The index page's plain HTML savings-account link is a decoy for this purpose (same product, different/older content) — the adapter only follows links whose href ends in .pdf.
